name: ethernet_cat6
_about: Ethernet cable held by the Franka, one end in the gripper, the rest hanging down and partly lying on the table. Numbers marked GUESS are typical Cat6 values to be replaced by measurements or identified by the bend sweep.

scan._frame: metres, in the scanner's own frame, as written by 04_pointcloud_vs_sim/tube_fit/fit_cable_tube.py. The scanner frame is usually NOT z-up.
scan._up: direction of 'up' in the scan frame. 'auto' = measured from the cable (it can only go down from the gripper, then lie flat on the table); or an axis 'z', 'y', '-y', ...; or a vector [x, y, z]. Everything is then turned so up is +z.
scan._gripper_end: auto = the higher end of the centreline (the other end lies on the table); or 'start' / 'end' of centerline.csv
scan._ground_z_m: null = lowest cable centreline point minus the radius (after turning up to +z); a number is in that turned frame

cable._radius_m: null = radius from summary.json (tube fit: 3.60 mm)
cable._mass_per_length_kg_m: GUESS: typical Cat6 patch cable 40-50 g/m. Weigh 1 m of your cable.
cable._bend_rigidity_EI_Nm2: GUESS from a physics estimate for a 7.2 mm Cat6: 8 solid copper wires of 0.57 mm (each 117 GPa x pi d^4/64 = 6e-4) ~5e-3, plus the PVC jacket 1-7e-3. The first guess, 1e-3, was clearly too soft (the sim hung straight down where the real cable bows out). MEASURE it: table-edge test, EI = w L^4 / (8 delta) with w = 0.44 N/m; e.g. 20 cm sticking out horizontally that drops 1.8 cm means EI = 5e-3.
cable._stretch_rigidity_EA_N: Real Cat6 is ~2e5 N (copper). 2e4 N is softer for a faster solve; stretch under own weight is still < 0.01 %.
cable._bend_damping_time_s: per-joint bend/twist damping = this x per-joint stiffness (the reference example uses 2e-3). Only changes how fast it settles.
cable._grip_length_m: length of cable inside the fingers, clamped (Franka finger pad ~2 cm). Added before the first scan node.
cable._plug_length_m: RJ45 plug + boot past the last scan node (the tube fit trimmed 36 mm there)
cable._plug_mass_kg: GUESS: RJ45 plug with boot 3-5 g. Spread over the plug segments.

contact._mu: GUESS: PVC jacket on a table
contact._self_collision: the scanned cable crosses itself; leave on so the strands cannot pass through each other

robot._enabled: the Franka is kinematic (does not move, only placed with IK). The cable boundary condition is the clamp, so the robot does not change the cable result.
robot._grasp: how the fingers hold the cable. 'across' = the finger pads pinch it from the sides, hand above the cable (like the reference example). 'along' = the cable comes straight out of the fingertips. Look at your scan/photo and pick the one that matches. Visual only.
robot._base_xyz_m: null = automatic: on the table, on the far side of the grip from the cable, facing it. The distances 0.4-0.7 m and both hand flips are tried, and the pose that reaches the grip with the arm highest above the table is kept. A value is in the SCAN's frame and metres (e.g. clicked in CloudCompare, divided by 1000 if the PLY is in mm).
robot._base_distance_m: first distance tried in automatic placement

sim._init: 'scan' = start the cable ON the scanned shape (rest shape stays straight) and let it settle: shows how far reality is from an equilibrium of this cable model. 'drop' = start straight and horizontal from the gripper and let it fall: shows path dependence of the part lying on the table.
sim._segment_length_m: ~2.8 x radius; check by halving it (convergence)
sim._friction_epsilon: VBD smooths friction below this sliding speed [m/s]. Newton's default 1e-2 lets a cable lying on the table creep ~1 mm/s forever; 1e-4 makes it stick (drift < 0.05 mm per 0.5 s).
sim._settle: settled = no centreline node moved more than settle_tol_m over the last settle_window_s (speed is not used: VBD velocities carry ~mm/s iteration noise even at rest)
sim._device: null = Warp default (cpu on a Mac, cuda:0 with an NVIDIA GPU)

sweep._bend_scale: multipliers on bend (and twist) rigidity, run with --sweep: EI = 1e-3, 2.5e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2, 2e-2 N m^2
